title: Analyzing and Graphing Compositions of f(x) = x - 7 and g(x) = x^2
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Let f(x) = x - 7 and g(x) = x^2. Find explicit formulas for the composite functions f o g and g o f, and describe the graphs of f, g, f o g, and g o f.

steps.title: Compute the Composite Formulas (f o g)(x) and (g o f)(x)
steps.mathExpression: (f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x)) = x^2 - 7, \qquad (g \circ f)(x) = g(f(x)) = (x - 7)^2 = x^2 - 14x + 49
steps.explanation: Substitute g(x) = x^2 into f(x) = x - 7 to obtain (f o g)(x) = x^2 - 7. Substitute f(x) = x - 7 into g(x) = x^2 to obtain (g o f)(x) = (x - 7)^2.
steps.why: Composing in opposite orders applies the shift -7 either after squaring (vertical shift) or before squaring (horizontal shift).

steps.title: Describe the Component Graphs f and g
steps.mathExpression: f(x) = x - 7 \text{ (line, slope } 1\text{, intercepts } (7, 0), (0, -7)\text{)}; \quad g(x) = x^2 \text{ (parabola, vertex } (0, 0)\text{)}
steps.explanation: The graph of f is a straight line with slope 1 shifted down 7 units from y = x. The graph of g is the standard upward-opening parabola with vertex at the origin (0, 0).
steps.why: Standard linear and quadratic parent curves.

steps.title: Compare the Shifted Parabola Graphs of f o g and g o f
steps.mathExpression: \begin{aligned} (f \circ g)(x) &= x^2 - 7 &&: \text{Parabola } y = x^2 \text{ shifted down } 7\text{, vertex } (0, -7),\text{ x-intercepts } (\pm\sqrt{7}, 0) \\ (g \circ f)(x) &= (x - 7)^2 &&: \text{Parabola } y = x^2 \text{ shifted right } 7\text{, vertex } (7, 0),\text{ y-intercept } (0, 49) \end{aligned}
steps.explanation: Both composite graphs are parabolas congruent to y = x^2: f o g shifts y = x^2 vertically downward by 7 units to vertex (0, -7) with range [-7, infinity), whereas g o f shifts y = x^2 horizontally right by 7 units to vertex (7, 0) with range [0, infinity).
steps.why: Post-composing with x - 7 produces a vertical shift down 7, whereas pre-composing with x - 7 produces a horizontal shift right 7.
